A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Conjuring Semantic Similarity by the same authors. All pages, including the appendices, are readable and support comparison; extracted content was checked against rendered equations, tables and figures.

before.justification: v2 reports original diffusion-model similarity scores, benchmark correlations, ablations and qualitative analyses in Tables 1–3, Figures 1–3 and Appendix A.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results, including diffusion-model benchmark scores, word-similarity analyses, ablations and appendix visualizations.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 retains the same paired denoising trajectories, squared score differences and Monte Carlo averaging. The divergence correction changes the mathematical description and normalization, while the implemented estimator, constant weighting and inference procedure remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate STS-B, STS12–16, SICK-R, RG65 and SimLex-999, with the same qualitative prompt cases. New Appendix B describes existing datasets rather than adding evaluated coverage.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 retain the same embedding and language-model comparators, four diffusion-derived baselines and text-encoder paragon. The newly cited MAUVE work is not added to the evaluated comparisons.

E3.justification: No previously stated experimental setting is revised: the Spearman metric, diffusion configuration, guidance scale, scheduler, image dimensions and ablation settings remain the same. Appendix B newly discloses dataset splits and sizes without establishing a protocol change.

E4.justification: The timestep-prior, Monte Carlo count, denoising-step and diffusion-model ablations, POS error analysis and qualitative cases are retained. Figure 2 presents the existing taxonomy analysis through reordered heatmaps and dendrograms, without changing its distances or substantive finding.

E5.justification: The numerical dispersion summaries remain, but v3 removes Section 4.3's explanation that the reported variability represents standard deviations across datasets. This reduces statistical-reporting context without changing estimates or adding repeated-run or seed information.

E6.justification: All entries in Tables 1–3 match, including the method's STS-B score of 70.3 and average of 65.4 ± 5.3. Figure 2's distances match after aligning word labels; Figure 3's results and Appendix A's visual examples are also retained.

T1.justification: Section 3.2 corrects the false Jensen–Shannon identification to Jeffreys divergence and replaces the half-weighted symmetric KL sum with the full sum. The revised Girsanov explanation also mistakenly attributes the martingale and vanishing-expectation argument to the stochastic integrand. The assumptions, SDEs and final estimator remain unchanged.

C1.justification: v3 narrows the framing toward interpreting image generators' learned semantic spaces and explicitly disclaims providing a superior general-purpose similarity metric. It removes the abstract's claim that textual representations lack fine granularity, while retaining the central visual-grounding, interpretability and human-alignment contributions.

C2.justification: Section 5 newly explains that generated images reveal the model's interpretation without resolving linguistic ambiguity. It removes the proposed mitigation through better LLM-based encoders, while Section 4.3 drops the argument connecting cross-dataset variability to subjective ground truth. Existing abstraction and computational-cost limitations remain.

D1.justification: New Appendix B documents STS-B's 1.5K-pair validation split, STS12–16 test splits and sizes, Spearman scaling by 100, and further dataset descriptions and an example. These improve documentation of existing experiments; Section 4.1's implementation, hardware and timing details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds Pillutla et al.'s MAUVE discussion and reference, and removes the BehnamGhader et al. LLM2Vec citation associated with encoder improvements. The introduction more explicitly relates the work to Liu et al.'s autoregressive meaning representations, already discussed in v2.

P1.justification: The introduction, derivation explanation and limitations receive localized rewrites, and Appendix B is added. Most prose and the main section sequence are retained, so this is not an extensive narrative reorganization.

P2.justification: The manuscript is globally retypeset into the ICLR format, changing the title and author arrangement, running headers, typography, paragraph spacing and float placement. Figure 2 is substantially redrawn with dendrograms, reordered axes and repositioned color bars; Figure 3 is relocated and Table 1's caption gains metric guidance.

improvement.justification: Correcting the divergence identification, documenting evaluation splits in Appendix B and explicitly acknowledging unresolved linguistic ambiguity improve precision and reproducibility. The net gain is modest: the algorithm and empirical evidence are retained, while the new integrand/martingale error in Section 3.2 and removal of Table 1's dispersion explanation introduce limited regressions.
